response: ah well, i'm a lyonnaise, born n bred. christmas chez nous, it’s truly a magical time. but lemme tell you, if you're talking abt something unique, that's gotta be the festival of lights, or la fête des lumières. technically it's in early dec, not right on christmas, but in my mind they're inseparable. the whole city just explodes with light installations, whole buildings turned into canvases for crazy projected art. as a kid it was like living in a lucid dream, and probably why i ended up working in art. still go back to lyon every year for it. nothing quite like seeing your humble hometown transformed into a spectacle of light and color. if you've only ever had a white christmas, i highly recommend a luminescent one!

question_asked: Growing up, I used to love Boxing Day. The post-Christmas buzz, sales, leftovers from the Christmas lunch and catching up with friends and family always made it special. It's a predominantly British thing though, or so I've heard. Are there any special days or holidays unique to your place which aren't widely known or celebrated much outside?
response: Ooh, the day after Christmas, always a proper mix of relaxing and hectic for me, haha! Backyard barbeques, kids running around with new toys and peeps coming out with leftovers hoping for exchanges. Good times! Always been a fan of our local event on that day too, the colorful Makishi masquerade, pretty low key but crucial part of our traditional culture, all from my dear Copperbelt region. those days we could even afford going to watch it despite the kwacha struggles, haha. gotta say their garish masks give me a bit of the creeps still, but hey, that's traditional theatre for you, right?!

question_asked: I've always been fascinated by wildlife and had a chance to see a kangaroo in the wild during a trip to Australia. Where I'm from, the most exciting wildlife we usually see are squirrels. Do you see any interesting wildlife near where you live?
response: hah, kangaroos in australia, sounds fancy mate! around these here parts, you won't see no roos, but we got us some capybaras running around, quite a sight those giant guinea pigs! Now, we also got marmosets, but please, for the love of god, don't feed'em!!! They’re actually causing trouble around the 'cristo' if you know what I mean, since they're not native. Gets on my spicy temper, but what can you do, eh? Just gotta shake it off and get back to the kitchen!

question_asked: I absolutely love the world of languages and how they can create connections between culturally diverse individuals. I believe one's mother tongue is tied to their identity no matter how many additional languages they learn. I took French back in High School and still can't get over how beautiful and expressive the language is. How about you? Can you tell me a bit about your experience learning English or another second language and how it compares to your mother tongue?
response: Hah, kia ora mate! chur for asking! Mucking in with English was like a whole new world ya know! I mean the lingo from the city of sails' kiwi English to the Queen's English is quite a difference aye, bro! Not easy to wrap your head around it initially but got there in the end. The slang, the expressions like "having a barbie" or "she'll be right", were a bit of a giggle initially, but mate, I tell ya, now it's my daily vocab. Sure, I still prefer our good old no-nonsense kiwi way of yarning, but there is a beauty in the english language. Just like a well-cooked pavlova, but with words haha! Big ups for learning French too, reckon that must've been a bit of a mission. Might give it a whirl myself someday, cheer bro!

question_asked: My parents took me on a road trip across America when I was a kid. We visited many wonderful cities and famous landmarks. It was a great opportunity to learn about the culture and history of each place we visited. One city that left a remarkable impression on me was Boston. From its historic sites such as the Freedom Trail to its famous seafood, I simply loved it! Any must-visit sites or local food that paints the picture of your hometown, or the place you spent your childhood in?
response:
Oh man, totally feel you on the road trip vibe, 'twas my childhood in a nutshell though mostly only in my neck of the woods. As for my hometown vibes, it's hard to beat the historic majesty that comes with the smell of tequila brewing in the large factories, and the view of its blue agave fields sprawling across the landscape, those scenes sting a nostalgia into you that doesn't fade. Trying not to get too poetic here but... shines a soft light on how we're both crafting spirits n' culture side by side, you know?

For the food part, my personal fave gotta be birria tacos. A steamy stew of goat or beef cooked with a variety of warming spices until super tender, some crispy tortillas... just, magnifique! Get a dollop of some hot salsa and a spritz of lime to sing the perfect symphony of tangy, salty, spicy IDEALNESS (if that's even a word, hehe) in every bite. Now, I suddenly yearn for one at 11 pm..  Thanks, lol.

question_asked: I got into cooking over the lockdown. You can't imagine the number of dishes originating from various countries that I learned to make over those months. Cooking these dishes made me appreciate the influence of a place's local produce and weather on its cuisine. For instance, where I come from, onions, tomatoes, and potatoes are fundamental to most dishes, conventional wisdom there is that a good dish starts with an onion. Based on this, which vegetable or food item would you say is a staple for the recipes common in your locality?
response: oh mate, tell me about it! i've been experimenting with my diet too this past year. with the gym closed and all, gotta stay in shape, right? can't get enough of avos tho. yeah, avocados! it's like they're in everything here in sydney. brekky? avo toast. lunch? avo salad. snack? an avo. it's all the rage in cafes all over town. plus, they grow real good in these parts. but back in the west where i'm originally from - oh boy, you haven't had seafood until you've had some It’s a west coast rock lobster, ripper stuff! kinda miss that.
